explication:
1. This is a TypeScript/Bun monorepo organized around one core product runtime and several adjacent surfaces. The main execution engine lives in `packages/opencode`, while `packages/app`, `packages/desktop`, `packages/web`, `packages/console`, `packages/enterprise`, `packages/ui`, `packages/sdk`, and `packages/plugin` provide alternate clients, cloud services, documentation, and integrations.

2. The heart of the system is `packages/opencode`: a terminal-native AI coding assistant. Its top-level flow is: CLI bootstrap → config/env loading → runtime initialization → server/session orchestration → provider calls and tool execution → persistence and resume. The runtime is designed around long-lived sessions, not short request/response cycles.

3. Session management is the core domain layer. `packages/opencode/src/session`, `actor`, `task`, `workflow`, `history`, `memory`, `inbox`, and `share` implement the long-horizon agent loop: prompt assembly, LLM request/response handling, checkpoints, compaction, retries, task trees, imports, and sharing. The README’s “persistent memory” and “automatic checkpoints” are backed by this layer.

4. The agent/tool boundary is explicit. `packages/opencode/src/tool` defines the available capabilities such as shell, file read/write/edit, git, ripgrep/search, LSP, MCP, web fetch/search, memory access, tasks, and workflows. Session code decides when to invoke tools; tool modules encapsulate the concrete side effects and permission checks.

5. Model/provider integration is another major boundary. `packages/opencode/src/provider` normalizes multiple LLM backends and their auth/model schemas, while `packages/opencode/src/plugin` adds provider-specific adapters and custom behaviors. This is what allows MiMo Auto, Xiaomi MiMo Platform OAuth, Claude imports, and OpenAI-compatible custom providers to coexist under one abstraction.

6. Persistent state is stored locally and is a first-class subsystem. `packages/opencode/src/storage` and the SQL schema files under `session`, `memory`, `task`, `workflow`, `sync`, and related modules indicate a SQLite-backed store with migrations. Memory and history use FTS-style search and are treated as durable context inputs for future sessions, not just logs.

7. The local UI is split across multiple shells. `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui` provides the terminal UI, `packages/desktop` wraps the same product in an Electron-style desktop shell, and `packages/app` contains a separate Solid/Vite web app that mirrors much of the session UI. These surfaces all sit above the same core session/service layer rather than reimplementing agent logic.

8. `packages/ui` is the shared presentation library. It contains reusable components, theming, i18n, and small interaction primitives used by the app/desktop/web surfaces. The architecture boundary here is “visual and interaction components only”; business logic stays in `opencode` or the product-specific apps.

9. `packages/console` is the cloud control plane for MiMoCode. It is an Astro/Vite app plus backend route handlers, auth, billing, model/provider management, workspace administration, and public marketing/docs endpoints. Unlike the local agent runtime, this side focuses on account lifecycle, subscriptions, rate limiting, provider routing, and enterprise features.

10. The console’s backend is split into `packages/console/core`, `function`, `mail`, and `resource`. `core` contains domain logic and database schema/migrations via Drizzle; `function` holds serverless helpers such as auth/log processing; `mail` renders transactional email templates; `resource` declares cloud resources. External dependencies here materially shape the architecture: OAuth, Stripe webhooks, provider APIs, and rate limit enforcement.

11. Sharing and enterprise distribution have their own surface area. `packages/enterprise` serves shared session/content views, while `packages/opencode/src/share` and the web app’s `pages/s/[id]` route support rendering exported conversations. This is a separate read-only publishing path from the interactive session runtime.

12. Integrations are packaged independently. `packages/plugin` is the generic plugin package, `sdks/vscode` is a VS Code extension, and `packages/extensions/zed` is a Zed integration. These consume the core runtime contracts but remain outside the local CLI/session implementation.

13. The documentation and public website are separate from the product runtime. `packages/web` is the Astro-based docs/marketing site with multilingual content, while `packages/console/app` also serves product-facing pages and docs routes for the cloud service. These sites are content-heavy and mostly consume shared share-rendering components rather than core agent logic.

14. Cross-cutting build and deployment concerns are centralized in the repo root. `sst.config.ts`, `infra/`, and the various `script/` and `packages/*/script` directories orchestrate cloud deployment, releases, code generation, and packaging. The repo uses Bun, Turborepo, Vite, Storybook, Playwright, and extensive tests to keep the local runtime, cloud control plane, and UI surfaces aligned.
